IMPLEMENT STORY #444: #427's gate reads one run form, and a lint failure's notes can lose the finding

You are implementing exactly one story from the code-health epic (#330) on branch story-444-lint-guard-and-notes, already checked out in this worktree off origin/main. The issue text below is the whole framing: its "What is asked" and "Acceptance" sections are what done means. Decision 0071 (the architectural principles) is ACCEPTED, and the house rules' Architecture section states its Rust form. Build to it. Where the issue leaves a choice to the operator, implement the option it recommends (or the first listed), keep it small, and say which you took in your result notes so the pull request can ask for the ruling. If the story is too large for one reviewable commit, deliver the smallest complete slice that meets acceptance items end to end, and name the rest in notes as follow-ups. Do not deliver a half-built everything.

RULES
- Scope: this story and nothing beside it. Follow-ups go in your notes, not in the diff. Prefer targeted edits over rewrites. A structural move keeps behaviour and bytes: every existing test keeps its name and its assertions unless the story says otherwise.
- A gate must be shown to bite: for every new check, plant the violation it exists to refuse, run the check and see it fail with the stated reason, then remove the plant. Record each removal control (what you planted, the command, the failure text) in your notes and in the commit message.
- Tests: assert exact values and exact error text, never is_err() alone. A new gate fails closed: read typed data where it exists; where you must scan text, refuse what the scanner does not recognise.
- Coverage: the repository enforces literal 100% line, branch and function coverage (scripts/coverage-exact.sh), which the controller runs after you; do not run that script. Keep every new production line and branch reachable by a test, and delete code you make unreachable.
- Frozen surfaces do not move: contracts/, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/. Decisions 0001 and 0003 stand. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063): add no Windows code.
- Every witness digest your change moves is re-pinned from the tests' own reported values, never computed by hand.
- Main requires twelve status checks; keep their names: "delivered by brokkr", "MSRV (1.88)", "format, clippy, contracts", "test (ubuntu-latest)", "test (macos-latest)", "exact coverage gate", "dependency licenses (cargo-deny)", "non-Rust lints", "baseline ratchets", "RustSec dependency audit", "release binary artifact", "mutants in the diff: brokkr-core". Three of them bite code moves:
  - baseline ratchets (quality/ratchet.sh, quality/README.md): lines per file at most max(baseline, 800) production and max(baseline, 2000) test; no new jscpd clone (50 tokens, 5 lines) in production, test or data. A repeated block needs a helper, not a copy. A function or file that is MOVED counts as new, so name any raised baseline in your notes for the PR's Ruling: line.
  - #337's suppressions: every suppression is #[expect(lint, reason = "...")], never #[allow]; quality/suppressions.txt must equal the tree. After adding or removing one, regenerate it with BROKKR_REGENERATE_SUPPRESSIONS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test suppressions, and remove an #[expect] your change leaves unfulfilled (clippy reports it). A shrink needs no ruling; a new suppression does.
  - mutants in the diff: brokkr-core: a brokkr-core change must not add a mutant no test catches (quality/mutants/brokkr-core.missed.txt is empty).
- Gates before you report complete, all clean, run from the worktree root:
  - cargo fmt --all -- --check
  - cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
  - cargo test -p <crate> for every crate you touched, and cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test suppressions
  - typos --hidden
  - quality/ratchet.sh files, and quality/ratchet.sh clones
  - shellcheck -S warning <each .sh you changed>, and actionlint if you touched .github/
  - git diff --check
- Commit when done: one commit, signed off (git commit -s), message "<area>: <what changed> (#444)" in the repository's style, ending with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push.
- Evidence: every claim in your notes points to a command you ran in this session and what it printed. Anything you did not observe is pending, not done.

HOST FACTS AND PARALLEL WORK

- Main is 07c78116 (2026-09-27). Tracks A (charter) and B (gates) have merged, including #342's budgets and #427 (scripts/lint-non-rust.sh, the one offline lint list that ci.yml and a landing's verify seat both run).
- Operator ruling, 2026-09-26, the threat model for every gate: catch realistic ACCIDENTAL misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read. A deliberate, exotic evasion is a LOW residual.
- Host tool versions, as ci.yml pins them: typos 1.50.2, shellcheck 0.11.0, zizmor 1.30.1, actionlint 1.7.12, lychee (setup-lychee's digest), jscpd 5.3.2, cargo-shear 1.14.0, cargo-crap 0.5.0, cargo-public-api 0.52.0, cargo-mutants 27.1.0, stable Rust 1.98.0 (rust-toolchain.toml), MSRV 1.88.0. CI runs actionlint with SHELLCHECK_OPTS='-S warning'; run it the same way.
- On this host typos, shellcheck, actionlint, zizmor and lychee live in ~/.local/bin, and jscpd, cargo-shear and cargo-crap in ~/.cargo/bin. In CI they are installed by the pinned install-action and setup-* actions.
- Other stories are implemented in parallel on other branches. Stay out of their files unless your story needs them, and say so in notes if it does:
  - #427 (verify seats run CI's offline checks): recipes/*/scripts/verify-seat.sh, recipes/*/README.md, .github/workflows/ci.yml's lint-non-rust job, and their tests.
  - #344 (operator commands as one module): crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine.rs's operator region, a new engine/operator.rs, crates/brokkr-core fold and a new OperatorCommand, and the CLI and bridge call sites.
  - Later, one at a time: #356 (Windows removal), #355 (retire unused), #354 (journal hot path) and #352 (one transcript path).
- This story follows #427 (PR #442, merged as 07c78116). Its review rated both items low and gave the fix shapes quoted in the issue.
- Changing recipes/fast/scripts/verify-seat.sh moves the digest of fast and of every recipe that extends it. Re-pin each witness from the tests' reported values, as #427 did.

THE ISSUE (#444), verbatim:

Part of epic #330, track B. Follow-ups from #427 (PR #442, run `implement-story-427-a-landing-vo-6aa0f028`), both rated low by its review.

1. **The guard on `ci.yml`'s lint job reads one form only.** `the_non_rust_lints_job_runs_every_check` (`crates/brokkr-cli/tests/workflow_pins.rs`) refuses a lint that runs beside `scripts/lint-non-rust.sh` only on lines that, trimmed, start with `run: `. A `- run: typos --hidden` step and a `run: |` block both pass it, and `ci.yml` uses `- run:` seven times. A sixth tool name is caught in no form.
   **Ask:** an allowlist of the job's run steps, read in every form (`run:`, `- run:`, block scalars), which refuses a form it cannot read.
2. **A lint failure's notes name the command but can lose the finding.** The script's closing `lint-non-rust: <command> failed` line always satisfies `failure_notes`' keyword grep in `recipes/fast/scripts/verify-seat.sh`, so the `tail -n 20` fallback never fires for a lint. A shellcheck warning or an actionlint finding carries no keyword, and it never reaches the notes. `recipes/landing/README.md` promises "the failing command and its decisive output".
   **Ask:** append the output's tail on every lint failure, and bind that with a stub whose output carries no keyword.

## Acceptance

- Plant `- run: typos --hidden` and a `run: |` block in the job: the workflow test fails on both.
- A stub shellcheck printing a real-format SC2086 warning yields verify notes that carry the file, line and code.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

result.notes:
Story #444 is committed as 089241b0 on story-444-lint-guard-and-notes. The commit is signed with the steward key (git log --show-signature printed G) and signed off. It is not pushed.

1. Lint-job guard (crates/brokkr-cli/tests/workflow_pins.rs). A new helper, run_steps, reads every run a job's steps carry: `run:` and `- run:` inline, and `|`/`>` block scalars with their chomping indicators. Any other form panics with "a run: this guard cannot read": empty, quoted, anchored, tagged, a flow mapping, or an indentation indicator. the_non_rust_lints_job_runs_every_check now holds the job's run steps to an exact allowlist of three: the list, the mermaid render and the Renovate validator. That replaces the per-tool `run: ` scan. Five job.contains fragments of those same three steps were dropped because the allowlist asserts them whole (ruling 5). This is a change to an existing test's assertions, made because the story asked for the allowlist. The uses: and fallback: checks stay.

2. Verify notes (recipes/fast/scripts/verify-seat.sh). failure_notes takes an optional `tail` argument that skips the keyword grep, so the existing fallback appends the output's tail. The lint call passes it. The existing typos test's expected notes did not change. New test: script_gates.rs a_lint_finding_without_an_error_word_reaches_the_landing_verify_notes, which uses a stub shellcheck printing SC2086 in its default tty format. SC2086 is labelled "(info)" there, as real shellcheck labels it; the stub prints it whatever -S says.

Removal controls, each planted in this session, run with cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test workflow_pins/script_gates, seen failing, then removed:
(a) `- run: typos --hidden` in the job: the_non_rust_lints_job_runs_every_check failed with an assert_eq whose left side carried "typos --hidden" as a step.
(b) a `run: |` block running typos --hidden: the same failure.
(c) `- run: "typos --hidden"`: panicked "a run: this guard cannot read".
(d) `- run: |2`: panicked the same way.
(e) the seat's `tail` argument removed: the new test failed, the notes carrying only the closing "lint-non-rust: ... failed" line.
ci.yml is back to its committed bytes: git status showed only the intended files.

Witnesses re-pinned from the tests' reported values: recipes/fast d242cc9a…, triage e3bc01e5… (in both compose_tests and witness_digests), night-shift 1c5a32fb…, wager-harness d3237bbe…, gpt-flash ecbe48a5…. No others moved.

Gates run in this session, all clean: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings; cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast (90 suites ok, no FAILED lines); cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test suppressions; typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files ("file size holds"); quality/ratchet.sh clones ("duplication holds"); shellcheck -S warning verify-seat.sh; git diff --check; compile --bundle bundles/self.

Pending: scripts/coverage-exact.sh, not run per framing. The diff adds no production Rust; only test files and a shell script. Remote CI is also pending.

Residuals (LOW, per the 2026-09-26 threat model): the guard skips a key spelled `run :` or `"run":`, since it only acts on lines containing `run:`. A line that contains `run:` inside some other value (for example a name) is refused, which fails closed. A lint whose output runs past 20 lines keeps only its last 20, as before. No suppressions, baselines or ratchets were raised.

cargo test --workspace: 90 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

members.adversarial: Reviewed the #444 diff: run_steps allowlist in crates/brokkr-cli/tests/workflow_pins.rs, the lint tail in recipes/fast/scripts/verify-seat.sh, the new script_gates test, and the re-pinned witness/compose digests. Independently reproduced every removal control: planting `- run: typos --hidden` and a `run: |` block in ci.yml's lint-non-rust job makes the_non_rust_lints_job_runs_every_check fail (left carries "typos --hidden"); `run: "..."`, `run: |2`, `run: !foo` and empty `run:` panic; removing the ` tail` argument from verify-seat.sh:64 makes a_lint_finding_without_an_error_word_reaches_the_landing_verify_notes fail with the SC2086 file/line/code absent. Witness/compose digest tests pass, quality/ratchet.sh files and clones hold, typos --hidden clean, shellcheck -S warning clean, git diff --check clean, working tree restored clean. Residual (low), no security hold: run_steps only recognises a run key when the raw line contains the literal `run:` (workflow_pins.rs:1465), so two valid YAML spellings that GitHub Actions and actionlint accept are silently skipped and the exact-allowlist assertion still passes. Inputs: planting `      - "run": typos --hidden` in ci.yml's lint-non-rust job -> `cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test workflow_pins the_non_rust_lints_job_runs_every_check` prints `test result: ok. 1 passed`; same for `      - run : typos --hidden`. python3 yaml resolves both to {'run': 'typos --hidden'} and `actionlint wf.yml` exits 0. The helper's doc comment claims a quoted run: form is refused; only quoted/anchored/tagged values are. This requires a deliberately exotic key spelling, so per the operator's 2026-09-26 threat model it is a low residual; every realistic form the story names fails closed.
members.correctness: Reviewed 089241b0 against origin/main, decision 0071 and #444. The exact run-step allowlist covers the requested `- run:` and `run: |` cases; the shellcheck stub asserts the failing command, file, line and SC2086 appear in verify notes. The commit records removal controls for both run forms, unreadable forms, and the notes tail. LOW residual (ruling 9, fail-closed text scanning): crates/brokkr-cli/tests/workflow_pins.rs:1465 searches only for `run:`, so a valid YAML step written `- run : typos --hidden` is silently ignored and the allowlist can pass. The repository's scripts/shellcheck-actions.sh:24 already recognizes `run :` as a form requiring refusal. This is an unusual syntax bypass under the stated accidental-misuse threat model, not a current ci.yml failure. `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` was clean; no tests were run by this read-only seat. The prior verify result reports pass, and the implement commit records its tests and gates.

result.notes:
